answer_1.quote: We explore the open and closed-source LLMs space ... evaluate them on the following sequence-to-sequence tasks, reframed as text generation tasks ...: text summarisation, text simplification, and grammatical error correction (GEC).
answer_1.outputs: generated text (summaries, simplified sentences, corrected sentences)

answer_2.quote: We used the most widely adopted reference-based metrics for each of the tasks. For text simplification, we report the SARI score. For text summarisation, we report the ROUGE score; ... For GEC, we report the F 0.5 score computed using the ERRANT toolkit.

answer_3.quote: We used GPT-4 as an additional reviewer to assess whether it can be reliably deployed in place of human reviewers. ... GPT-4 was also asked to annotate the same 100 samples that were shown to human reviewers for each of the three tasks.

answer_4.quote: Due to budgetary and time constraints, we recruited 3 human reviewers through the Prolific platform and asked them to review the quality of the models' outputs ... For human evaluation of text summarisation, we followed the evaluation criteria ... Relevance, Fluency, Coherence and Consistency ... For text simplification, we followed the evaluation criteria ... Semantics, Fluency and Simplicity ... For GEC, we adopted the Over‑correction criterion ... and introduced two new criteria: Semantics and Grammaticality.
answer_4.guideline: Evaluation criteria and definitions for each task were provided to annotators (e.g., Relevance, Fluency, Coherence, Consistency for summarisation; Semantics, Fluency, Simplicity for simplification; Semantics, Grammaticality, Over‑correction for GEC) using a 5‑point Likert scale.
